name: geant4_depth_dose_simulation
description: Monte Carlo depth-dose simulation with GEANT4: fire a particle beam into a slab of one NIST material and get the energy deposited in each depth bin, plus the peak depth (the Bragg peak for ions). Use it for range and shielding questions — how deep a 150 MeV proton beam deposits its dose in water, how much of a gamma beam a lead slab absorbs, how an ion's range changes with energy or tissue. One fixed application is compiled against the local GEANT4 on first use; nothing but the numbers below can vary, so no geometry or macro is accepted. Requires a local GEANT4 installation with its physics data (geant4-config on PATH, or GEANT4_CONFIG set); a 200-event proton run takes about a second.

energy_mev.description: Kinetic energy of each primary particle in MeV, from 0.001 to 100000 (default 150).

material.description: Target material, a NIST name GEANT4 builds itself (default 'G4_WATER').

thickness_cm.description: Depth of the target along the beam in cm, from 0.01 to 500 (default 20). Make it larger than the expected range, or the beam leaves the target before stopping.

bins.description: Number of equal depth bins to score, from 1 to 2000 (default 100). thickness_cm / bins is the depth resolution.

events.description: Primary particles to simulate, from 1 to 200000 (default 200). More events mean a smoother curve and a longer run.

timeout_seconds.description: Give up after this many seconds, from 1 to 1800 (default 600).

oneOf.description: One finished Monte Carlo depth-dose run.

status.description: 'success' when the simulation ran and scored.

material.description: The NIST material the beam was fired into, echoing the request, e.g. 'G4_WATER'.

particle.description: The beam particle, echoing the request, e.g. 'proton'.

energy_mev.description: Kinetic energy of each primary particle, in MeV.

events.description: How many primary particles were fired. The curve is a sum over all of them, and its statistical noise falls with this number, so two runs at different `events` are not comparable bin by bin.

thickness_cm.description: Depth of the slab, in cm. A beam whose range exceeds it leaves through the far face and its dose is not scored.

bin_width_cm.description: Depth of each bin, in cm: thickness_cm divided by the number of bins. Every depth in this reply is a multiple of it, so it is also the resolution of the peak position.

total_edep_mev.description: Energy deposited in the whole slab, in MeV, summed over all events. Less than events x energy_mev whenever anything escaped.

edep_mev_per_bin.description: Energy deposited in each depth bin, in MeV, ordered from the entrance face. This is the depth-dose curve itself; bin i spans depths i*bin_width_cm to (i+1)*bin_width_cm.

items.description: Energy deposited in one bin, in MeV.

geant4_version.description: The GEANT4 the application was compiled against, as geant4-config reports it. Physics models change between versions, so a curve is only reproducible with it.

summary.description: What a depth-dose curve is usually read for. EVERY KEY HERE IS CONDITIONAL: the peak keys are present only when the run returned bins and a bin width, last_depth_with_dose_cm only when some bin is non-zero, and edep_mev_per_event only when events is non-zero -- so an absent key means the curve could not support it, not a value of zero.

peak_bin.description: Index of the bin holding the most energy. For an ion beam this is the Bragg peak.

peak_depth_cm.description: Depth of the CENTRE of that bin, in cm. Resolved only to bin_width_cm, so a peak depth quoted more precisely than that is spurious.

peak_edep_mev.description: Energy deposited in the peak bin, in MeV.

last_depth_with_dose_cm.description: The far edge of the deepest bin with any dose: the practical range in this material. Equal to thickness_cm means the beam was not stopped by the slab, so the real range is greater and this run does not measure it.

edep_mev_per_event.description: total_edep_mev divided by events: the energy one primary particle leaves behind on average, which is the figure that compares across runs of different size.

oneOf.description: The simulation did not run or did not finish.

error.description: Why there is no curve: a rejected argument, a missing GEANT4 installation or physics data, a build failure, or the timeout.
